meta.title: Silver City — Annals Alley
meta.subtitle: Secular Roman and Jewish historians confirm Jesus Christ's historical existence.
meta.blurb: Skeptics say Jesus Christ never existed. Annals Alley opens hostile Roman and Jewish historians—Tacitus, Josephus, and Suetonius—who record His execution under Pilate and the early stir of His name in Rome.
meta.notes: Generated from street book. Engine maps lesson fields 1:1 to Learn / Match / Hold / Journal.

lesson.ideaLabel: Tacitus wrote that Christus was executed under Pontius Pilate.

learn.shortStory: Tacitus was a famous Roman historian who did not follow Jesus. Yet he wrote that Christus was executed under Pontius Pilate in Judea. Even hostile writers in ancient Rome recorded that Jesus was a real person.

learn.gloss: Tacitus wrote that Christus was executed under Pontius Pilate.
learn.loci: This idea lives in Annals Alley, with Silas Whitman.

word.sense: Roman historian who documented Jesus' execution under Pilate.

learn.hint: Keep the Roman report of Pilate. Toss the claim that Jesus was made up much later.

lesson.ideaLabel: Suetonius wrote that Claudius expelled Jews from Rome over Chrestus.

learn.shortStory: Suetonius was an imperial biographer who wrote the lives of twelve Roman emperors. He wrote that Emperor Claudius banished Jews from Rome because of riots over "Chrestus." This shows that belief in Jesus reached Rome within two decades of His resurrection.
learn.mainIdea: Suetonius wrote that Claudius expelled Jews from Rome over Chrestus.

learn.loci: This idea lives in Annals Alley, with Silas Whitman.

learn.hint: Keep the Roman biographer's account of Claudius. Toss the claim that Christians only reached Rome centuries later.
